+# Per-alphabet tables are cached in plain dicts (importing functools for
+# lru_cache costs more than the lookups it saves); each cache is cleared
+# once it holds _CACHE_SIZE entries so it stays bounded.
+_CACHE_SIZE = 128
+_encode_pairs_cache = {}  # type: dict
+_decode_map_cache = {}  # type: dict
+_decode_table_cache = {}  # type: dict
+
+
+def _cache_store(cache: dict, key: object, value: object) -> None:
+    if len(cache) >= _CACHE_SIZE:
+        cache.clear()
+    cache[key] = value
+
+
+def _get_base58_encode_pairs(alphabet: bytes) -> List[bytes]:
+    try:
+        return _encode_pairs_cache[alphabet]
+    except KeyError:
+        pass
+    # pairs[hi * base + lo] is the two character encoding of digits hi, lo
+    pairs = list(map(bytes, product(alphabet, repeat=2)))
+    _cache_store(_encode_pairs_cache, alphabet, pairs)
+    return pairs

actions.reason: Replace functools.lru_cache on the three per-alphabet table builders (_get_base58_encode_pairs, _get_base58_decode_map, _get_base58_decode_table) with module-level dict caches. functools is not otherwise imported by the module's dependencies, and importing it pulls in collections, reprlib, types and others at import time; this cost dominates the savings lru_cache provides. Caches are keyed exactly as before ((alphabet) and (alphabet, autofix)), remain bounded at 128 entries (cleared when full), and unhashable keys still raise TypeError. Encoding/decoding logic is unchanged; equivalence harness reports identical outputs. Measured: check_ir 0.9589, encode_ir 0.9659, decode_ir 0.9757.
